title: Species classifiers for microcontrollers
subtitle: int8 MobileNetV2 species classifiers for TFLite Micro and the Coral Edge TPU, companions to Google's AIY models
description:
# Model Summary

Species classifiers small enough for microcontrollers and the Coral Edge TPU, companions to Google's AIY Vision Kit iNaturalist models (google/aiy on Kaggle). MobileNetV2 1.0 at 160 px, full-integer int8, one deployment contract. Four variations: mammals (246 species), arachnids (153), herps (483 reptiles and amphibians) and fungi (341). The fungi model is not for edibility decisions. Source, scripts and the GitHub release with checksums: https://github.com/mlgraham/species-classifiers

# Model Characteristics

Stock tf.keras MobileNetV2, no custom ops. Each variation ships int8 (uint8 in/out), the same model compiled with Edge TPU compiler 16.0 (every op mapped), float32, labels.txt and classes.json. Ethos-U55 builds for the Seeed Grove Vision AI V2 are in the GitHub release.

# Data Overview

Trained on the iNaturalist 2021 competition dataset's train split (mammals 68,917 images, arachnids 40,687, herps 133,082, fungi 90,048), validated on its val split (10 images per species).

# Evaluation Results

int8 file, 87.5% centre crop: mammals 54.9% top-1 / 80.5% top-5 (grayscale 44.9% / 73.2%); arachnids 62.3% / 86.4%; herps 46.0% / 74.4% (grayscale 34.4% / 62.7%), below the 55% bar set for it before training, so treat it as a first cut; fungi 74.0% / 93.5%. Google's stock AIY insect model scores 59.1% top-1 on the iNat2021 species it shares, choosing among 1,022 classes.
